scope: Cut Textbutler pickup latency without changing the Ghostget connector: (a) a drained event starts its run as soon as its debounce elapses instead of waiting for the next provider poll tick; (b) the automatic reply path's pre-claim capability and grant gates opt into sharing one in-flight provider status read and reusing a success for up to 10 seconds, instead of spending two serialized native iMessage sessions on the same answer. Owner-initiated checks keep reading fresh.

motivation.liveTimeline: Owner self-chat probe on the deployed pilot: chat.db row 0.2s, Ghostget event stored 7.4s, run claimed 21.9s, ack in chat.db 40.9s. Native helper timeline showed the drain at ~7s, the run starting only after the next poll tick (~13.5s), then a capability status session (+14.4s) and a grant status session (+19.2s), each queued behind poll-loop sessions, before the claim.
motivation.steadyStatePoll: With host load normal the poll tick costs ~6.5s (status + scoped events native sessions plus host admission gaps).

design.debounceDispatch: tickOnce arms a single timer at the earliest pending eligibleAt. dispatchDue starts a run only for contacts the latest poll marked healthy and initialized, that are active at the same settings revision, not running, not blocked, and have no uncertain send; it re-arms if a newer message moved the window. Uninitialized, unhealthy, blocked or fenced contacts stay with the poll tick, which alone snapshots and reconciles. A failed tick clears health. Close disarms the timer. Loops constructed with automatic:false arm nothing unless a test injects scheduleDispatch.
design.statusReuse: Reuse is opt-in per call through a maxAgeMs bound capped at STATUS_REUSE_MS=10000; callers that omit it (owner capabilities, owner sends, setup) read fresh exactly as before, and a fresh success refreshes the shared entry. Only the automatic transport capability gate and ControlService.delegatedGrant (via OwnerAutomationPort.grantStatus maxStatusAgeMs) opt in. Only successes are reused, measured from completion; a failed read evicts the entry. Concurrent opted-in callers share one invoke that carries no single caller's signal; a caller's abort rejects only that caller. start() evicts. Ghostget still re-authorizes and re-checks provider identity inside every dispatch.
design.unchanged: Journal claim, intent/ack ordering, uncertain-send fencing, grant renewal, disclosure, and all transport retry arbitration are unchanged. No connector, enrollment, grant or provider route changes.

independentReview.method: Implementer self-review of the full diff only. No separate agent review was performed for this change.

coverage: an elapsed debounce starts the run without waiting for another provider poll (no extra pollSet/events call; one status read before claim)
the debounce dispatch never starts a paused, fenced or not-yet-due contact (early fire re-arms; pause wins; unreconciled send stays with the poll tick)
provider status reuse is opt-in, shared in flight, bounded, and never keeps a failure (fresh owner reads see a changed account; tighter bounds honored; per-caller abort)
owner-messages: capabilities bind the live account and detect an account change on the next owner check (this caught and shaped the opt-in design)

aggregateValidation.note: An earlier aggregate run found that unconditional status reuse hid an owner-visible account change (owner-messages.test.ts); reuse was made opt-in and that suite now passes in the focused command. CI on the pull request is the aggregate record.

limitations: Post-claim latency (ack and reply dispatch chains inside Ghostget, ~1.5-2s of host admission per native session) is unchanged and needs a connector change.
A reused status can be up to 10s old for pre-claim gates; dispatch-time identity checks inside Ghostget remain authoritative.
No live messaging was performed for this evidence; live verification follows deployment.
